scope: All 14 samples previously assigned good in hopper-bad-20261023/review.json
method: Independent source, managed IL, decoded JavaScript and native entry-path inspection; fresh archive/resource/hash checks; official-release and npm comparisons; existing VirusTotal file and behavior reports queried by hash only. No specimen or installer was executed as a host process and no file was uploaded to VirusTotal. Isolated Atoms string-decoder evaluation performed no application/OS/network actions.
interpretation: Good is an artifact-intent/training label, not endpoint deployment authorization, vulnerability clearance, vendor false-positive resolution, or an unconditional allowlist. Antivirus disagreement is explicitly retained.
scanner_status: No taxonomy change was justified by this verification. Prior final scans had no hostile finding in all 14 and one accurate suspicious Defender-exclusion finding in Sleipnir. Prior make validate and 60 focused boundaries passed; those tests were not rerun for evidence-only report changes.

samples.assessment: Legitimate remote-administration artifact; deployment intent is unknown.
evidence: Re-extracted all 35 MSI compound streams and decoded the nine-row CustomAction table. Actions call ScreenConnect managed entry points or WiX service configuration; the one launch action targets the packaged ScreenConnect client.

Re-extracted SfxCA and inspected all 33 managed methods, including FixupServiceArguments, CheckMsiFileName, CheckMsiMotw and TerminateProcesses. Parameter merging, installer-origin reporting and termination of ScreenConnect helper processes explain the actions.

Client/service assemblies and tenant configuration are coherent with ScreenConnect. The earlier independent review verified DigitalSignature, MsiDigitalSignatureEx and the ConnectWise certificate chain for this exact SHA256; the new VT record also reports a valid ConnectWise signature.
limits: The signature verification was performed in the prior exact-hash review, not rerun with osslsigncode in this pass.
7z still reports a checksum warning for Client.en-US.resources. It is a CAB resource warning, not UPX packing/checksum failure. The warning is retained in the evidence.
An unauthorized installation of this privileged unattended client can be an incident. A signed legitimate RMM artifact does not establish tenant ownership or installation consent.
samples.endpoint_disposition: Confirm approved deployment and tenant ownership if discovered unexpectedly; retain good as the software-artifact label.

samples.assessment: Likely antivirus false positive for a security-sensitive optimizer.
evidence: Fresh extraction reproduces the sole embedded Sleipnir.ps1 resource. The PE entry method reads that named resource and feeds it into a PowerShell runspace; the 120-method wrapper is consistent with PS2EXE hosting and console/UI plumbing.

Inspected the 5710-line script. Gaming/maximum profile UI actions call Add-DefenderExclusions for game paths and processes. Other changes have explicit tweak/profile handlers and local backup/restore functionality.

Driver installation downloads through an explicit UI action, requires HTTPS, a valid Authenticode signature with expected vendor naming and a successful restore point before starting the installer. The placeholder self-download URL is rejected while unchanged.
Existing VT behavior (powercfg, bcdedit, compact/dism and Add-Type compilation) matches the visible optimizer operations. The accurate suspicious Defender-exclusion trait remains enabled.
limits: VT reports 26 malicious detections; these have not been cleared by vendors.
The executable signer is a self-issued Sleipnir Local Publisher certificate with an untrusted root, not a verified publisher identity.

The script can weaken protection and disrupt host settings. Its comment about preventing cross-host HTTP redirects is stronger than its actual implementation. No blanket safety or security-quality endorsement is made.
samples.endpoint_disposition: Investigate an unexpected installation and review applied exclusions; observed behavior supports optimizer intent rather than hidden theft.

samples.assessment: Likely antivirus false positive for the inspected preview installer.
evidence: Fresh managed-resource extraction matches the prior extraction. Recomputed the payload archive SHA256 and all 226 manifest member hashes; no extra archive members exist.

Reviewed the 34 installer methods and the native-host managed IL. Installer verifies payload integrity and confines destination paths. Packaged application contains a PDF reader, WebView2 bridge and Google Drive integration.

The bridge is bound to the local virtual origin https://ieo.example/ and dispatches named reader/settings/OAuth operations. Google scopes are drive.file and drive.appdata; token exchange targets Google. Startup registration is a settings-controlled HKCU Run entry for the installed application, with a corresponding removal path.
Existing VT behavior reflects application installation and shortcuts/startup handling; it does not establish an unrelated payload.
limits: VT reports 13 malicious detections, chiefly generic/ML names. The inner ieo-native.exe hash is absent from VT (HTTP 404), which is not a clean verdict.
Manifest consistency proves packaging integrity, not publisher trust. No trusted publisher signature was established.
The reader and bundled third-party JavaScript were not exhaustively audited for vulnerabilities or every feature.
samples.endpoint_disposition: Likely benign reader installation based on recovered behavior; investigate deployment provenance if unexpected.

samples.assessment: Likely antivirus false positive despite substantial engine disagreement.
evidence: Fresh extraction verifies the embedded app.pak SHA256, then decodes its gzip/custom asset container into index.html, player.html and PeerJS. All 17 managed methods were inspected.

Decoded 10979 JavaScript string-wrapper calls using only the isolated string decoder and rotation logic. Inspected file-save, device-key, media, plugin and network paths; application code was not run.

Native loopback handlers validate Host and Sec-Fetch-Site; sensitive POST handlers require X-Atoms: 1. Save targets are restricted to configured roots with filename/path checks. The DPAPI-protected value is the application device key. Prior-instance termination targets the same executable identity.

Decoded application functionality is encrypted peer-to-peer social/chat/calling. Network paths include the local helper, PeerJS broker and atomsconnections.com version/plugin catalog. Plugin downloads have catalog hash checks and iframe execution uses allow-scripts without allow-same-origin. Media capture is associated with calling/test controls.
VT sandbox behavior showing a loopback browser launch, WMI and DPAPI is accounted for by the inspected native methods. No independent hidden credential collector or unrelated payload was found.
limits: VT reports 31 malicious detections, including Qwexlafiba and GenericKD; the disagreement is unresolved with vendors.
X-Atoms: 1 is a fixed header, not a secret authentication token. This corrects the previous review wording.
No trusted publisher signature or exact official-release binary comparison was established. Plugins, external services and the entire cryptographic/security design are not certified by this review.
samples.endpoint_disposition: Likely benign application based on decoded behavior; the detection volume warrants confirming deployment provenance, not an unconditional allowlist.

samples.identity: FRP 0.71.1 Darwin amd64 client npm wrapper

samples.identity: CAP tester server 0.1.1 Darwin arm64 npm wrapper
samples.assessment: Published CAP tester package, consistent with its advertised developer-test purpose.
evidence: Archive has only package.json and the native server, with no lifecycle hooks or dependencies. Original tarball SHA512 matches npm dist.integrity.
Fetched server source at the npm gitHead 86dd1f1b3555b921eb4bd3929380d3ada010a751. Routes, messages and configuration in the binary match the published file/TCP/UDP/Zenoh test interfaces.
Source defaults to 127.0.0.1:4173, supports explicit host/port overrides and optional Basic authentication. Broad file/network access is the advertised capability-testing interface.
limits: No reproducible native build comparison was performed. Published checksums prove registry identity, not absence of malicious code.
The server can read/write arbitrary paths and manipulate sockets. Exposing it beyond loopback without authentication changes the deployment risk.
samples.endpoint_disposition: Developer capability-test server is the supported identity; investigate an unexplained or externally exposed instance.

samples.assessment: Benign explicit remote-module helper, with dangerous capability if misused.
evidence: Read all six wheel members; verified all populated RECORD hashes and sizes. No .pth, entry point or lifecycle hook is present.
Remote retrieval and exec(compile(...)) occur only through explicit obtain/dispatch calls with a caller URL or MODELWORKS_URL. There is no fixed attacker endpoint or import-time download/execution.
limits: Calling the API trusts remote Python code. Good labels the observed artifact intent, not the safety of invoking it with arbitrary URLs.
samples.endpoint_disposition: Inspect the caller and configured URL if execution is unexplained; this package itself does not establish a concealed supply-chain payload.

samples.assessment: Strong evidence for a benign integration-test binary.
evidence: Traced native entry 0x140dbe92c through CRT main 0x14009a6b0 and Rust main 0x14006da70. Rust main passes the table at 0x140dceb40 and count 40 to the test-main routine at 0x140101590.

Decoded all 40 reachable test descriptors, including their function/name/source structure. Test names concern stale selections, bounded file providers, resumable acquisition, retention and authorization invariants; source locations point into Syncliva acquisition tests.
VT reports zero malicious and 71 undetected engines, corroborating rather than establishing the verdict.
limits: This is an entry-path/descriptor and supporting-code review, not a source-reproducible build or proof of every linked dependency. The misleading malware-family filename is not a behavioral finding.
samples.endpoint_disposition: Development/test artifact is the supported identity; check why it was present if the host is not a development machine.

samples.assessment: Likely antivirus false positive for the inspected trading application installer.
evidence: Re-extracted with collision preservation. Both installer entries named MT5MasterPro.exe are identical (SHA256 6fa5fb6f40aad7d9d2dffb5460641dfeff38837a1584656dbe6289aa6c097c89). The earlier overwrite did not hide a distinct executable.

Built innoextract with debug metadata output and inspected installer tables: no compiled Pascal code, five application file-association registry entries, and one post-install application launch that is skipped for silent installs and runs as the original user.

Inspected the recovered .NET application IL and its update/account/WebView paths. UpdateButton_Click downloads the installer and InstallNowButton_Click launches the selected downloaded installer with a visible runas prompt. Trading/OAuth/WebView functionality is coherent with the application.
limits: VT reports eight malicious detections in the same MSILHeracles adware cluster; these are unresolved. The main managed DLL is absent from VT (HTTP 404), not cleared by VT.
No trusted publisher signature was established. This review does not establish the legitimacy of the trading business, financial claims, remote account service, or future updates.
samples.endpoint_disposition: Likely benign software artifact; deployment provenance and business trust remain separate questions.

integrity_checks.registry_entries: Five application file-association entries; no Run-key entry

samples.assessment: Benign standalone source fragment with an unsafe callable capability.
evidence: Read the complete 95-byte file. It defines serve_asset($asset), echoes file_get_contents($asset), and then require_once($asset).
There is no invocation, request-input source, hardcoded payload or hidden execution trigger in this file.
limits: An application that passes attacker-controlled paths can turn the helper into an inclusion vulnerability. The caller is not supplied.
samples.endpoint_disposition: Review callers and input validation if deployed; the isolated definition is not evidence of a web shell.

samples.identity: Adult-site HTML snapshot with commented CoinHive code
samples.assessment: Benign captured page for malware-intent labeling; mining text is inactive.
evidence: Parsed HTML script/comment boundaries instead of relying on keyword matches. Both CoinHive constructors, their script include and start calls are in HTML comments; none is in an executable script block.
The 24 live script blocks contain UI libraries/handlers, analytics, advertising, reCAPTCHA, Facebook and Baidu integration. No active inline miner or exploit was identified.
limits: External advertising/script resources were not fetched. The static snapshot verdict does not certify current remote content or the site itself.
samples.endpoint_disposition: A page/cache artifact with inactive miner snippets, not an active miner on the evidence supplied.
